prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1311; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant's account changed in important ways between conversations: the direction of the impact and the number of people in the car are now different.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a left-turn collision at an intersection. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office. Initial file set up and photos requested.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and that coverage was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start. Police report requested.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witness statements received. Witnesses, scene photos and the other driver all confirm the collision happened as the claimant described. The police and witnesses also confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 4: Reported knee injury is consistent with the mechanism of a crash like this one. Medical records show treatment ran somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the records obtained so far.

Entry 5: Second recorded conversation with the claimant's attorney present. The account has shifted in important ways from the first call, including the direction the vehicle was struck from and the number of occupants. Clarification requested in writing. No earlier vehicle damage is known from prior claims or inspection notes.

Entry 6: Repair estimate and inspection reviewed. It is not yet clear whether all listed damage resulted from this impact, so a separate review of the damage pattern has been requested. Claim remains open pending the reconciled account and that review.
